prompts.text: Name an enzyme activity labeling one of the ten standard steps of human glycolysis. Isoenzymes for the same step count as one answer.
prompts.explanation: Complete ten-step bank. This prompt credits reaction activities, not distinct isoenzyme genes. Hexokinase and glucokinase are NOT biochemical synonyms; either earns the same step-1 credit by explicit prompt scope. PFK-2, PDH and lactate dehydrogenase do not catalyze one of these ten steps.
prompts.scope: Complete ten-step bank. This prompt credits reaction activities, not distinct isoenzyme genes. Hexokinase and glucokinase are NOT biochemical synonyms; either earns the same step-1 credit by explicit prompt scope. PFK-2, PDH and lactate dehydrogenase do not catalyze one of these ten steps.
references: MILEDOWN PDF p.87 (glycolysis diagram); KAPLAN_BIOCHEM_2023 pp.525–534

answers.label: Phosphofructokinase-1
answers.explanation: Committed regulatory step and prominent study anchor; usually recalled early.

answers.label: Hexokinase activity
answers.explanation: First pathway step; glucokinase is an accepted step-equivalent isoenzyme response, not a synonym.

answers.label: Pyruvate kinase
answers.explanation: Memorable ATP-producing terminal step, but less immediate than PFK-1.

answers.label: Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase
answers.explanation: NADH-generating step is emphasized; long name reduces spontaneous production.

answers.label: Fructose-bisphosphate aldolase
answers.explanation: Recognizable cleavage step but less salient than irreversible steps.

answers.label: Glucose-6-phosphate isomerase
answers.explanation: Standard reversible conversion; full-name recall is less automatic.

answers.label: Phosphoglycerate kinase
answers.explanation: Important substrate-level ATP step: high educational yield does not guarantee quick name recall.

answers.label: Enolase
answers.explanation: Named dehydration step, moderately emphasized but not a first-choice anchor.

answers.label: Triose-phosphate isomerase
answers.explanation: Standard pathway member with lower spontaneous salience.

answers.label: Phosphoglycerate mutase
answers.explanation: Less prominent reversible rearrangement; PGM accepted only in this glycolysis context, not glycogen context.

prompts.text: Name a standard proteinogenic amino acid whose side chain contains an aromatic ring.
prompts.explanation: Four chemically aromatic side chains: phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan AND histidine (aromatic imidazole). Introductory charts often file histidine under basic rather than aromatic, but those categories are not chemically exclusive. Standard 20 only; no nonstandard analogues.

answers.explanation: Canonical benzene-containing aromatic amino acid.

answers.label: Histidine
answers.explanation: Chemically aromatic imidazole, usually taught under basic side chains. Very high MCAT yield but low spontaneous recall to the aromatic prompt; this is an intentionally surprising correct answer.

prompts.text: Name a psychological defense mechanism.
prompts.explanation: Fourteen source-supported examples, not an exhaustive universal taxonomy. Other valid mechanisms must be reviewed rather than labeled scientifically wrong. Coping/defense categories vary; suppression is consciously postponing attention to a distressing thought, not proof that it becomes unconscious.
prompts.scope: Fourteen source-supported examples, not an exhaustive universal taxonomy. Other valid mechanisms must be reviewed rather than labeled scientifically wrong. Coping/defense categories vary; suppression is consciously postponing attention to a distressing thought, not proof that it becomes unconscious.
references: KA_PS PDF pp.155–156; parsed imported Anki fields corroborate individual terms (source-match-preview.json)

answers.label: Denial
answers.explanation: Everyday label and foundational example.

answers.label: Repression
answers.explanation: Foundational unconscious exclusion of distressing content; distinct from suppression.

answers.label: Projection
answers.explanation: Commonly taught attribution of unacceptable feelings to someone else.

answers.label: Displacement
answers.explanation: Redirecting affect toward a safer target; standard vignette.

answers.label: Rationalization
answers.explanation: Self-protective explanation for behavior; standard vignette, tied with two equally salient examples.

answers.label: Sublimation
answers.explanation: Channeling impulses into socially acceptable activity is a standard mature-defense example.

answers.label: Regression
answers.explanation: Return to an earlier behavioral pattern under stress.

answers.label: Reaction formation
answers.explanation: Expressing the opposite of an unacceptable impulse; needs a clear definition.

answers.label: Intellectualization
answers.explanation: Focusing on abstraction to distance affect; not automatically the same as isolation of affect.

answers.label: Suppression
answers.explanation: Conscious setting aside, often confused with repression. Lower spontaneous recall despite clear distinction.

answers.label: Humor
answers.explanation: A defense-function use of humor, not every joke; less obvious as a technical category.

answers.label: Altruism
answers.explanation: Service to others can function as a mature defense; the prompt-specific role matters, not every helping act.

answers.label: Passive aggression
answers.explanation: Indirect expression of hostility; less often first produced as a defense label.

answers.label: Projective identification
answers.explanation: More specialized interpersonal defense involving projection and the other person being induced to experience/embody projected material. Not an alias of projection; supplied notes p.155 explicitly discuss it.

prompts.text: Name one of the three standard intermolecular attraction categories between neutral molecules used in introductory MCAT chemistry.
prompts.explanation: Complete conventional three-category introductory set: dispersion, permanent dipole–dipole, and hydrogen bonding. The classification explicitly includes hydrogen bonding separately despite its relationship to electrostatic dipolar interactions. Ion–dipole is outside this neutral-molecule scope. This is not a full microscopic taxonomy.
prompts.scope: Complete conventional three-category introductory set: dispersion, permanent dipole–dipole, and hydrogen bonding. The classification explicitly includes hydrogen bonding separately despite its relationship to electrostatic dipolar interactions. Ion–dipole is outside this neutral-molecule scope. This is not a full microscopic taxonomy.

answers.label: Hydrogen bonding
answers.explanation: Highly familiar biomolecular interaction.

answers.label: London dispersion forces
answers.explanation: Standard universal attraction, with many names for the same category.

answers.label: Permanent dipole–dipole interactions
answers.explanation: Standard attraction between permanent dipoles. Do not accept bare van der Waals as a unique synonym: it can cover multiple categories.

prompts.text: Name a carboxylic-acid derivative functional-group family used in organic or biochemical acyl-transfer reactions. Count cyclic members within their parent family.
prompts.explanation: Five core families identified and validated here, not a claim that no other acyl derivative exists. Family names are required; specific substrates such as acetyl-CoA or acetyl chloride prompt clarification to thioester/acyl-halide family. Acyl phosphates belong to mixed anhydrides in this family-level bank; no independent extra credit. Carboxylic acid itself is the parent, not an answer.

Acyl phosphates belong to mixed anhydrides in this family-level bank; no independent extra credit. Carboxylic acid itself is the parent, not an answer.

answers.label: Ester
answers.explanation: Prominent oxygen-linked acyl derivative; a lactone is a cyclic ester, not a second family.

answers.label: Amide
answers.explanation: Prominent peptide-related acyl derivative; lactams count within this family.

answers.label: Acid anhydride
answers.explanation: Named acyl derivative, less immediate than ester/amide; mixed anhydride cases need context.

answers.label: Thioester
answers.explanation: Important in acetyl-CoA biochemistry yet less likely to be volunteered to an organic derivative prompt.

answers.label: Acyl halide
answers.explanation: Common in broader OChem but less emphasized in the MCAT-specific derivative chapters. The weighted formula can rank it rarer than thioesters despite easier recall—a model concern.

prompts.text: Name a simple first-order proton NMR multiplicity produced by coupling to one set of n equivalent spin-½ neighbors, for n from 0 through 6.
prompts.explanation: Complete seven-answer n+1 bank under the stated idealized coupling model. Do not include multiplet, octet, dd or dt: generic/compound patterns or n=7 are outside this scope. Septet/heptet are aliases. Equivalent protons do not ordinarily split one another.

answers.explanation: Zero equivalent coupling neighbors, one line.

answers.explanation: Six equivalent neighbors, seven lines. Isopropyl examples make it more salient than a generic sextet despite higher n.

answers.label: Quintet
answers.explanation: Four equivalent neighbors, five lines; less routinely named.

answers.label: Sextet
answers.explanation: Five equivalent neighbors, six lines; textbook pattern less often encountered.
